keyRules: In the Open Category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point on the Earth’s surface—not simply straight down, so near a slope the terrain beside you can also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the entity responsible for the obstacle may request authorization to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle’s height.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or can transfer more than 80 J of impact energy)—this applies even to toys. Below 250 g, registration is still required if the drone has a sensor able to capture personal data, unless it is considered a toy under the European Toy Safety Directive. Pilot training/certificate requirements are separate and depend on the drone’s class and subcategory.
In Portugal, the minimum age to fly independently in the Open Category is 16. The A1/A3 training and exam are free, taken online, and valid for 5 years.
Third-party liability insurance is mandatory for drones with an MTOM over 900 g (Decreto-Lei n.º 58/2018); the minimum coverage, conditions and capital are set out in Portaria n.º 2/2021.

Flying over sovereign bodies, embassies and consulates, military installations, facilities of the security forces and services, and prisons is prohibited unless authorized by the responsible entity (ANAC Regulamento n.º 1093/2016, kept in force by Decreto-Lei n.º 87/2021). The Sintra-Cascais Natural Park requires authorization from the ICNF.

In the Open Category, you must keep the drone within your own direct visual line of sight, with the naked eye (glasses/contact lenses are acceptable; binoculars or a screen do not count)—or fly with the help of an observer, maintaining clear and effective communication between you at all times so that together you can monitor the airspace and avoid collisions. Follow-me mode is a separate exception, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.
Do not fly in airport and heliport protection zones (CTR/ATZ) without authorization—check the zones on the app’s map and at dnt.anac.pt.
Night flights are permitted in the Open Category without ANAC authorization—turn on a flashing green light on the drone.
Azores and Madeira: Additional regional restrictions may apply

Capturing aerial images requires prior authorization from the Autoridade Aeronáutica Nacional (AAN) via the e-AAN platform—the only channel for aerial surveys. The application must be submitted at least 10 days before the activity begins; the maximum period granted is 30 consecutive days (AAN’s Guia Rápido e-AAN).
importantNotes: Portugal has a dual system: ANAC regulates flights, while AAN authorizes the capture of aerial imagery.
Registration is free and valid in all EU/EASA countries
Mandatory insurance for drones weighing more than 900 g
Flying over military installations, prisons, and embassies is prohibited; flights in areas under military jurisdiction require authorization from the AAN.
Wildfire Season: Additional Restrictions May Apply to the Use of Drones
The GDPR applies to the collection of identifiable images
